She thanks the student who points it out.
She stops the race entirely.
She removes that student from the team.

questions.evidence:
When the class chooses a captain for its puzzle race, everyone expects loud, quick-speaking Rex to lead. Instead, the teacher asks quiet Nori to try. Rex looks disappointed and says the team may waste time if nobody gives immediate orders.

At the first station, Nori asks each member what they notice. One sees a number pattern, another spots a word hidden in the instructions, and Rex finds a shortcut between two clues. Nori repeats the ideas clearly and asks which ones can be checked.

The team loses a minute testing a wrong pattern, then corrects it because someone feels comfortable pointing out the mistake. Nori thanks that student instead of defending the first idea. Rex begins asking questions too, and the last station goes smoothly.

They finish second. On the way back, Rex says winning would have been nice, but he had not expected so many useful ideas to come from listening. Nori smiles and asks him to lead the next practice using the same approach. The captain's job, they discover, can be to make other people's thinking visible.
questions.explanation: 隊長促進每人想法被看見、驗證及修正。
options: Giving orders faster than anyone else.
Preventing teammates from mentioning mistakes.
Helping the team express and check its ideas.
Measuring success only by finishing first.
questions.prompt: What kind of leadership does the story emphasize?

lessons.story:
When the class chooses a captain for its puzzle race, everyone expects loud, quick-speaking Rex to lead. Instead, the teacher asks quiet Nori to try. Rex looks disappointed and says the team may waste time if nobody gives immediate orders.

At the first station, Nori asks each member what they notice. One sees a number pattern, another spots a word hidden in the instructions, and Rex finds a shortcut between two clues. Nori repeats the ideas clearly and asks which ones can be checked.

The team loses a minute testing a wrong pattern, then corrects it because someone feels comfortable pointing out the mistake. Nori thanks that student instead of defending the first idea. Rex begins asking questions too, and the last station goes smoothly.

They finish second. On the way back, Rex says winning would have been nice, but he had not expected so many useful ideas to come from listening. Nori smiles and asks him to lead the next practice using the same approach. The captain's job, they discover, can be to make other people's thinking visible.
lessons.title: A Different Kind of Team Captain
